answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake in a shared kernel registry before it may trade. Creating thousands of fake accounts then costs real capital per identity, and misbehavior lets honest peers slash the bond. Think of the registry as a wharf: every vessel must pay a berth fee and show papers before docking, so a fleet of paper boats cannot flood the harbor. An ivory-tower design that trusts self-declared reputation without a stake invites cheap forgery; a bonded registry makes each fake identity expensive to mint and cheap to punish.
